title: On Marriage
attribution_note: St Ambrose of Optina (1812–1891). His letters and advice to spouses and parents. Translated here fresh from the Russian for this edition. Source: https://azbyka.ru/otechnik/Amvrosij_Optinskij/sovety-suprugam-i-roditeljam/1

sections.heading: Happiness is founded on the fear of God

pairs.en: On Marriage
Happiness is founded on the fear of God

I congratulate you on the newly-wedded, and N on his new wife. I heartily wish them mutual union and peace in marriage. And to you I wish comfort in their good obedience. May they show you the due respect and reverence that befits parents from sensible and obedient children. But all three of you must always remember this. Never forget it. Only then will your life pass peacefully and well — when we do not cast off God or forget Him. He is our Creator, our Redeemer, and the Giver of blessings both now and forever. And not to forget Him means to strive to live by His divine, life-giving commandments. And when we break them through our weakness, we must repent sincerely. Then we must at once set about correcting our mistakes and our straying from God's commands.
May the all-good Lord establish us on His saving path!

sections.heading: On bearing the burdens of family life

pairs.en: On bearing the burdens of family life

Family burdens must be borne as a lot we freely chose for ourselves. Second thoughts here do more harm than good. The only thing that helps is to pray to God for yourself and your family. Pray that He do what is useful for us according to His holy will.

From the heart I wish you everything you expressed in your short note. You asked for true understanding of affairs, gentle dealings with others, patient bearing of sorrows, and sensible repelling of human intrigues and the snares of the ancient enemy. Remember King David. With God's help he passed through like circumstances and wrote: "I waited patiently for the Lord, and He heard me and listened to my prayer, and brought me up from the pit of passions and from the mire of sinful clay, and set my feet upon a rock — the commandments of God — and directed my steps, and put a new song in my mouth, a hymn to our God" [Ps. 39:1–4].

sections.heading: It is impossible to live without clashes

pairs.en: It is impossible to live without clashes

You write to me about an incident that made an unpleasant impression on all of you. What is to be done? People of old decided long ago that you cannot get through life without a proverb. And they added that even a pot bumps into a pot. So how much more can people living together avoid bumping into each other? And this happens especially from different ways of looking at things. One person thinks about the course of affairs this way, another that way. One is convinced by notions that seem to him solid and well-founded, while another trusts in his own understanding. If in the first rule of arithmetic you add one and one, you get two. But if in the rule of three you multiply two by two, you get four. And if it comes to fractions, you find numbers on top and bottom with a line between them. So it is with human affairs. If they get too divided, you find inconvenience on top and below, with some barrier in between.

As I wrote and told you before, so I say again now. If you believe in God's providence and hope in His all-powerful help, you will meet no inconvenience and will always enjoy such peace of soul as is possible. But when you worry about things that may not even happen — for suppositions are mostly wrong and mistaken — you will only trouble yourself for nothing.

You are thinking: what if they suddenly refuse you? From the letters I receive I see no hint of this. And I do not think they would treat you so — except perhaps due to some special unforeseen circumstances. People propose all sorts of things. It does not always come to anything....

And I advise you to hold to the golden mean in dealing with younger and older. Try not to insist on your own way. Do your duty as far as reason allows, guided by the fear of God and your own conscience.
I call down peace and God's blessing on you. I remain with sincere good wishes for everything that profits your soul. External inconveniences must be endured.

sections.heading: On the need to endure with patience

pairs.en: On the need to endure with patience

You expected comfort and got distress instead. What is to be done? Do not be downcast. Comfort yourself with this thought. You are no better than holy King David. All his life long he suffered family troubles and sorrows — a hundred times worse than yours, I dare say. I will not describe them all. But I will say this much. His son Absalom resolved to throw his father from the royal throne and tried to take his life. Yet holy David sincerely humbled himself before God and before men. He did not reject Shimei's abusive reproaches. Instead, acknowledging his own guilt before God, he said humbly to others that the Lord had commanded Shimei to curse David. For such humility the Lord not only showed him mercy but restored the kingdom to him.

We must be sensible. That is, we must care first of all about obtaining God's mercy and eternal salvation. We must not care about restoring the former kingdom — that is, temporal goods that slip and keep slipping from a son's weakened hands. Yet the Lord is strong enough to amend him too, if only he will bend under God's mighty hand. We must pray to God humbly and with faith, that He instruct both him and us.

sections.heading: How prosperity and abundance spoil people

pairs.en: How prosperity and abundance spoil people

As for N, our words were passed on correctly. O. A. advised you to frighten her with the monastery, to keep her from trying to return to her parents' home for a certain reason. Thank God N stayed living with her husband, even in need. But plenty and abundance spoil people. From fat, as the proverb says, even beasts go mad.

sections.heading: On the Lord's ban on divorce

pairs.en: On the Lord's ban on divorce

N tells you that divorce between spouses is forbidden by the Lord Jesus Christ. We read the Lord's own words: "But I say to you: whoever divorces his wife, except for the cause of sexual immorality, gives her occasion to commit adultery" [Matt. 5:32].

From this everyone can see that the Lord did not forbid divorce without exception. If spouses keep faith with each other, they should not divorce. But if not, it is not fitting to bind them together. The Holy Church follows this rule....

sections.heading: Comfort and counsel for an abandoned wife

pairs.en: Comfort and counsel for an abandoned wife

You write that your husband sent you away. You have no proper refuge such as you would wish, and so you grieve. You have resolved to turn to God and ask Him, on the strength of the gospel words: "Ask, and it will be given you" [Matt. 7:7]. Well then — ask. Ask with certainty and patience. You will receive.

Only be wise about what you ask. He said: "Seek first the Kingdom of God and His righteousness, and all this" — that is, temporal, earthly things — "will be added to you" [Matt. 6:33]. He teaches us to pray like this: "Your kingdom come, Your will be done" [Matt. 6:10]. And "Enter by the narrow gate into the heavenly Kingdom" [Matt. 7:13]. And holy apostle James says: "You do not have, because you do not ask. You ask and do not receive, because you ask wrongly, to spend it on your pleasures" [James 4:2–3].

So ask the Lord for patience. He will give it to you. He will strengthen you on the path that leads to the heavenly Kingdom. He says: "I am the way and the truth" [John 14:6]. You do not know God's intentions for yourself. So pray: let His holy will be done upon you. On that lay your trust and hope humbly.

sections.heading: Pray to God for a husband who drinks

pairs.en: Pray to God for a husband who drinks

Your husband gives himself too much to drinking. And you treat him harshly — you beat him when he is drunk. Beating will not knock anything out of him. You will only make him more resentful. Better to pray for him with faith and earnestness. Pray to holy John the Baptist and the martyr Boniface. Ask that the all-good Lord, for the sake of His saints, turn him from the path of ruin and bring him back to the path of sober, restrained living.

sections.heading: On marriage between close blood relatives

pairs.en: On marriage between close blood relatives

You ask about the marriage of a nephew and niece who are related, saying that nowadays it is permitted. Well, what good is it that it is permitted? There is no marital happiness in it. And it shows up in the children as incurable sickliness. So I cannot advise entering into such marriages.

sections.heading: A Catholic married to an Orthodox woman

pairs.en: A Catholic married to an Orthodox woman

If you are willing to accept the truth of Orthodoxy, you should accept it without any conditions — as truth. But you write: "I am ready to fulfil my wife's wish, but only on condition that, having sacrificed my conviction, I see her in full health."

To this I tell you that this condition is quite out of place. Perhaps your wife's illness came about through your own fault. Perhaps you did not observe the feast days in your married relations. Or perhaps you did not keep married faithfulness. For this you are punished by your wife's illnesses, since a husband likes to have a healthy wife always. If you sincerely try to amend your life and sincerely accept the truth of the Orthodox confession, the Lord is strong enough to restore health to your wife — if only it is useful for you both. The all-good Lord always arranges only what is useful, profitable for the soul, and saving.
The Lord says of Himself in the Gospel: "I am the way and the truth and the life" [John 14:6]. Pray sincerely and with faith to the all-good Lord, that He lead you onto the true path of salvation.
